Internal Medicine.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 116/72 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, Temp 36.9 C. Mild suprapubic tenderness on palpation; no flank or costovertebral angle tenderness. Urine dipstick positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrites. Advised increased water intake and completing short antibiotic course.

medications.instructions: Dissolve sachet in a glass of water and drink on an empty stomach before bedtime.
Take after meals; turns urine orange-red.

Internal Medicine.prescriptionNotes: Drink at least 2 liters of water daily; return if fever or back pain develops.

Internal Medicine.chiefComplaint: Facial pressure, frontal headache, and blocked nose for four days.
Internal Medicine.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 122/80 mmHg, HR 76 bpm, Temp 37.4 C. Nasal mucosa edematous with clear mucoid discharge. Mild tenderness over maxillary and frontal sinuses. Tympanic membranes normal, lungs clear. Symptoms under 5 days without double sickening; supportive therapy initiated.

medications.instructions: Take for headache or facial pain.
Do not exceed 5 days to avoid rebound congestion.

Internal Medicine.prescriptionNotes: Use steam inhalation and saline rinses alongside nasal spray.

Internal Medicine.chiefComplaint: Dry nagging cough and mild chest soreness following a recent cold.
Internal Medicine.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, Temp 36.9 C, RR 16/min, SpO2 98%. Chest auscultation shows occasional scattered rhonchi clearing with cough, no crackles or focal consolidation. Pharynx mildly hyperemic. Reassured cough may take up to two weeks to settle.

medications.instructions: Take orally for dry cough, especially at bedtime.
Take with a full glass of water.

Internal Medicine.prescriptionNotes: Avoid smoke exposure and return if fever or shortness of breath develops.

Internal Medicine.chiefComplaint: Nausea and three episodes of vomiting since early morning.
Internal Medicine.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 114/72 mmHg, HR 86 bpm, Temp 37.1 C. Abdomen soft, mild epigastric discomfort, normal bowel sounds, no guarding. No diarrhea or severe abdominal pain. Administered oral antiemetic guidance and gradual clear fluid rehydration.

medications.instructions: Allow tablet to dissolve or swallow with minimal water.
Wait 30 minutes after antiemetic before sipping.

Internal Medicine.prescriptionNotes: Advance to bland solids once vomiting stops for 6 hours.

Internal Medicine.chiefComplaint: Brief spinning dizziness when rolling over in bed since yesterday.
Internal Medicine.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 74 bpm, SpO2 99%. Cranial nerves intact, normal gait and cerebellar finger-to-nose testing. Dix-Hallpike maneuver positive on right side with brief torsional upbeating nystagmus and vertigo. Performed Epley canalith repositioning maneuver in clinic with good tolerance.

medications.instructions: Take orally with food for residual dizziness.

Internal Medicine.prescriptionNotes: Sleep with head slightly elevated tonight and avoid sudden head tilts.

Internal Medicine.chiefComplaint: Low-grade fever, fatigue, and generalized muscle aches for two days.
Internal Medicine.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 88 bpm, Temp 38.0 C, SpO2 99%. Alert and oriented, no meningeal signs, no rash. Pharynx minimally injected, lungs clear, abdomen soft and non-tender. Advised rest, fluids, and antipyretics; monitor for focal symptoms.

medications.instructions: Take with water for fever or myalgia.

Internal Medicine.prescriptionNotes: Return if fever persists beyond 4 days or new focal symptoms appear.

Internal Medicine.chiefComplaint: Cramping lower abdominal pain, bloating, and hard infrequent stools for four days.
Internal Medicine.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 120/78 mmHg, HR 74 bpm, Temp 36.8 C. Abdomen mildly distended, soft, mild left lower quadrant tenderness with palpable fecal loading, normal bowel sounds, no rebound. Advised increased dietary fiber, water intake, and short-term osmotic laxative.

medications.instructions: Take orally with a glass of water; adjust after soft stool.
Take for abdominal cramping.

Internal Medicine.prescriptionNotes: Increase daily water intake and include vegetables and whole grains.

Ophthalmology.chiefComplaint: Red watery gritty eyes in both eyes for two days following a mild cold.
Ophthalmology.clinicalNotes: Visual acuity 6/6 OU. Pupils equal, round, reactive to light. Conjunctival injection with watery discharge and follicular reaction bilaterally; corneas clear on slit-lamp exam, no fluorescein staining. Preauricular node mildly tender. Advised cold compresses, artificial tears, and strict hygiene.

medications.instructions: Instill for comfort; avoid touching dropper tip to eye.

Ophthalmology.prescriptionNotes: Highly contagious; wash hands frequently and do not share towels or pillows.

Ophthalmology.chiefComplaint: Intensely itchy watery red eyes since yesterday after dusty wind.
Ophthalmology.clinicalNotes: Visual acuity 6/6 OU. Mild bilateral eyelid edema, conjunctival chemosis, and papillary reaction on upper tarsal conjunctiva; clear corneas, no mucopurulent discharge. Advised cool compresses, avoiding eye rubbing, and dual-action antihistamine/mast-cell stabilizer drops.

medications.instructions: Wait 5 minutes before using any other eye drops.

Ophthalmology.prescriptionNotes: Do not rub eyes; wear wraparound sunglasses outdoors during dusty weather.

Ophthalmology.chiefComplaint: Painful tender red bump on the right upper eyelid margin for two days.
Ophthalmology.clinicalNotes: Visual acuity 6/6 OU. Localized tender erythematous nodule at the right upper lash line pointing externally. Conjunctiva mildly injected nearby, cornea clear, extraocular movements full and painless. Advised warm compresses and topical antibiotic ointment.

medications.instructions: Apply along eyelid margin after 10-minute warm compress.

Ophthalmology.prescriptionNotes: Never squeeze the bump; discard old eye makeup.

Ophthalmology.chiefComplaint: Sudden gritty pain and tearing in the left eye after dust blew in outdoors.
Ophthalmology.clinicalNotes: Visual acuity 6/6 OU. Everted left upper eyelid revealed a tiny dark dust particle on subtarsal conjunctiva; removed cleanly with moistened cotton swab under topical anesthetic. Fluorescein staining negative for corneal abrasion; anterior chamber quiet. Prescribed short-course lubricating and antibiotic drops.

medications.instructions: Instill into lower conjunctival sac.

Ophthalmology.prescriptionNotes: Avoid rubbing eye; return if pain, photophobia, or blurred vision develops.

Ophthalmology.chiefComplaint: Right eye redness and thick yellow discharge sticking eyelashes together this morning.
Ophthalmology.clinicalNotes: Visual acuity 6/6 OU. Diffuse right conjunctival injection with mucopurulent discharge at medial canthus and lashes. Cornea clear without ulceration or fluorescein uptake; anterior chamber deep and quiet. Advised cleaning lids with sterile saline and broad-spectrum topical antibiotic.

medications.instructions: Clean discharge gently with warm water before instilling.

Ophthalmology.prescriptionNotes: Avoid contact lenses until fully resolved for at least 48 hours.

Ophthalmology.chiefComplaint: Alarmed by a painless bright red spot on the white of the left eye since morning.
Ophthalmology.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 122/78 mmHg. Visual acuity 6/6 OU. Well-demarcated bright red subconjunctival hemorrhage in temporal quadrant of left eye following a coughing spell. Cornea clear, pupils reactive, normal intraocular pressure by palpation. Reassured blood will resorb over 1 to 2 weeks.

medications.instructions: Use only if mild fullness or scratchiness is felt.

Ophthalmology.prescriptionNotes: No specific treatment needed; return only if eye pain or vision change occurs.

Ophthalmology.chiefComplaint: Burning tired eyes and mild blurriness after long hours on a computer screen.
Ophthalmology.diagnosis: Acute digital eye strain and tear film instability
Ophthalmology.clinicalNotes: Visual acuity 6/6 OU. Reduced blink rate noted; mild conjunctival redness, shortened tear breakup time, negative corneal staining. Fundus and pupils normal. Counseled on the 20-20-20 visual break rule, screen positioning, and preservative-free lubricants.

medications.instructions: Instill during screen work and before sleep.

Ophthalmology.prescriptionNotes: Look 20 feet away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes of screen use.

Ophthalmology.chiefComplaint: Sharp scratching sensation in the right eye after a child's fingernail grazed it.
Ophthalmology.clinicalNotes: Visual acuity 6/6 OU. Slit-lamp exam with fluorescein shows a small 2 mm linear epithelial defect on inferior right cornea without infiltrate or stromal involvement; anterior chamber quiet. Prescribed topical antibiotic prophylaxis and lubricant; no patching needed.

medications.instructions: Complete full 5 days to prevent infection.
Apply before sleep for overnight corneal protection.

Ophthalmology.prescriptionNotes: Return in 48 hours for recheck, or sooner if pain worsens.

Ophthalmology.chiefComplaint: Crusty flaky eyelashes and mild burning in both eyes upon waking for one week.
Ophthalmology.clinicalNotes: Visual acuity 6/6 OU. Mild erythema of eyelid margins with cylindrical collarettes at lash bases; corneas clear, mild tear film debris. Educated on daily warm compresses and dilute lid margin hygiene.

medications.instructions: Apply after cleaning eyelid margins with warm damp pad.

Ophthalmology.prescriptionNotes: Perform warm compresses and gentle lid scrubs twice daily.

Ophthalmology.chiefComplaint: Puffy itchy left upper eyelid after a mosquito bite last night.
Ophthalmology.clinicalNotes: Visual acuity 6/6 OU. Soft non-tender edema of left upper eyelid with a central bite punctum; no erythema spreading past orbital rim, normal extraocular movements, no pain with eye movement, no proptosis. Advised cool compresses and oral antihistamine.

medications.instructions: Take orally to reduce swelling and itching.

Ophthalmology.prescriptionNotes: Return immediately if eyelid becomes hot, painful, or vision blurs.

Orthopedics.chiefComplaint: Twisted right ankle during a football match yesterday with outer ankle swelling.
Orthopedics.diagnosis: Acute grade I right lateral ankle sprain
Orthopedics.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 76 bpm. Mild swelling and tenderness over the anterior talofibular ligament. Able to bear weight with mild limp; no bony tenderness over medial or lateral malleoli, navicular, or fifth metatarsal base (Ottawa criteria negative). Neurovascularly intact. Advised rest, ice, compression, and elevation.

medications.instructions: Take after meals.
Apply gently over lateral ankle.

Orthopedics.prescriptionNotes: Use elastic ankle support during walking; avoid sports for 2 weeks.

Orthopedics.chiefComplaint: Sudden lower back pain and stiffness after lifting a heavy box this morning.
Orthopedics.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 124/78 mmHg, HR 80 bpm. Paraspinal muscle spasm and tenderness at L4-L5 level without midline bony tenderness. Straight leg raise negative bilaterally; lower limb motor strength 5/5, sensation intact, symmetric reflexes. No red flags. Advised staying gently active and avoiding bed rest.

medications.instructions: Take orally after meals.
May cause mild drowsiness; avoid driving if affected.

Orthopedics.prescriptionNotes: Apply warm compresses for 15 minutes twice daily; avoid heavy lifting.

Orthopedics.chiefComplaint: Painful right wrist after a minor slip on an outstretched hand yesterday.
Orthopedics.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 74 bpm. Mild dorsal wrist swelling and tenderness. Anatomical snuffbox non-tender; distal radius and ulna non-tender; full finger flexion and intact radial pulse. Right wrist X-ray shows no fracture or carpal malalignment. Provided removable wrist splint.

medications.instructions: Take after meals with water.

Orthopedics.prescriptionNotes: Wear wrist splint during daytime activities for 7 days.

Orthopedics.chiefComplaint: Woke up with severe right-sided neck stiffness and pain when turning the head.
Orthopedics.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 118/76 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, Temp 36.7 C. Head slightly tilted to right; palpable spasm in right sternocleidomastoid and upper trapezius. No cervical spine tenderness, no radicular arm pain, upper limb neurological exam normal. Advised gentle range-of-motion stretching and local heat.

medications.instructions: Take after meals.
Take before sleep as it may cause drowsiness.

Orthopedics.prescriptionNotes: Use a supportive single pillow and apply warm compress to neck.

Orthopedics.chiefComplaint: Aching pain on the outer right elbow for one week after painting walls.
Orthopedics.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 122/78 mmHg, HR 72 bpm. Point tenderness over the right lateral epicondyle; pain reproduced by resisted wrist extension with elbow extended. Full elbow flexion and extension, intact distal neurovascular status. Advised activity modification and counterforce forearm strap.

medications.instructions: Massage gently over outer elbow; wash hands after use.
Take for aching pain.

Orthopedics.prescriptionNotes: Avoid repetitive gripping and wringing motions for 2 weeks.

Orthopedics.chiefComplaint: Front knee ache when climbing stairs for five days after a long hike.
Orthopedics.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 70 bpm. No joint effusion, no joint-line tenderness. Mild peripatellar tenderness and pain with resisted knee extension; Lachman and McMurray tests negative. Advised icing after activity and temporary reduction of stair climbing.

medications.instructions: Take orally after breakfast.

Orthopedics.prescriptionNotes: Begin gentle isometric quadriceps sets once acute pain settles.

Orthopedics.chiefComplaint: Painful bruised left big toe after stubbing it against furniture this morning.
Orthopedics.diagnosis: Acute soft-tissue contusion of left hallux
Orthopedics.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 76 bpm. Mild dorsal bruising and swelling over proximal phalanx of left great toe; no subungual hematoma, intact skin, normal capillary refill. Toe X-ray negative for fracture. Advised wide-toe-box footwear and icing.

medications.instructions: Take orally for pain.

Orthopedics.prescriptionNotes: Apply ice pack wrapped in cloth for 15 minutes three times daily.

Orthopedics.chiefComplaint: Right shoulder ache when reaching overhead after intense swimming.
Orthopedics.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 122/76 mmHg, HR 72 bpm. No deformity or swelling. Painful arc between 70 and 120 degrees abduction, mild tenderness over supraspinatus insertion, intact rotator cuff strength 5/5. Advised relative rest from overhead strokes and ice application.

medications.instructions: Take orally with food.

Orthopedics.prescriptionNotes: Perform gentle pendulum exercises; avoid overhead lifting for 10 days.

Orthopedics.chiefComplaint: Sharp heel pain on first morning steps after walking extensively in flat sandals.
Orthopedics.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 120/78 mmHg, HR 74 bpm. Localized tenderness at the medial calcaneal tubercle; pain exacerbated by passive toe dorsiflexion. Normal ankle range of motion and intact sensation. Advised supportive cushioned footwear, calf stretching, and rolling foot over a cold bottle.

medications.instructions: Take after meals.

Orthopedics.prescriptionNotes: Avoid walking barefoot on hard tiled floors; use silicone heel cup.

Orthopedics.chiefComplaint: Tender swollen lump on the front of the right shin after bumping a table.
Orthopedics.clinicalNotes: Vitals: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 74 bpm. Localized 3 cm ecchymosis and soft-tissue tenderness over mid-anterior right tibia; skin intact, no crepitus, full painless knee and ankle motion, intact distal pulses. Advised ice packs and leg elevation.

medications.instructions: Apply gently over bruised area; do not rub vigorously.

Orthopedics.prescriptionNotes: Return if swelling expands rapidly or skin breaks down.

Pediatrics.chiefComplaint: Four-year-old child brought by mother with fever and right ear pain since last night.
Pediatrics.clinicalNotes: Weight 16 kg. Vitals: Temp 38.4 C, HR 118 bpm, RR 24/min, SpO2 99%. Child alert, crying when right tragus pressed. Otoscopy reveals bulging, erythematous right tympanic membrane with loss of light reflex; left ear normal. Throat mildly red, chest clear. Prescribed weight-based antibiotic and analgesic.

medications.medicationName: Amoxicillin / Clavulanic acid 457 mg/5 ml suspension
medications.instructions: Shake well; give at the start of a meal (45 mg/kg/day amoxicillin).
Give for fever above 38 C or ear pain (15 mg/kg/dose).

Pediatrics.prescriptionNotes: Complete full 7-day antibiotic course; return if fever persists after 48 hours.

Pediatrics.chiefComplaint: Two-year-old child brought by father with four watery stools today and reduced appetite.
Pediatrics.diagnosis: Acute pediatric gastroenteritis with mild dehydration
Pediatrics.clinicalNotes: Weight 12 kg. Vitals: Temp 37.5 C, HR 122 bpm, RR 26/min. Alert, slightly dry lips, normal skin turgor, tears present, capillary refill under 2 seconds. Abdomen soft, non-tender, hyperactive bowel sounds. Advised oral rehydration therapy and zinc supplementation.

medications.instructions: Dissolve 1 sachet in 200 ml clean water; give with spoon or cup.
Give orally after feeding.

Pediatrics.prescriptionNotes: Continue age-appropriate feeding; return if sunken eyes, lethargy, or persistent vomiting occurs.

Pediatrics.chiefComplaint: Six-year-old child brought by mother with barking cough and hoarse voice since midnight.
Pediatrics.clinicalNotes: Weight 20 kg. Vitals: Temp 37.8 C, HR 110 bpm, RR 22/min, SpO2 98%. Playful, no stridor at rest, no suprasternal retractions, mild barking cough on crying. Lungs clear bilaterally with good air entry. Administered single oral corticosteroid dose and educated on cool mist.

medications.instructions: Give orally once (0.15 mg/kg single dose).
Give for fever or throat discomfort.

Pediatrics.prescriptionNotes: Seek urgent care if noisy breathing at rest or difficulty breathing develops.

Pediatrics.chiefComplaint: Eight-year-old child brought by parents with high fever and painful swallowing for two days.
Pediatrics.clinicalNotes: Weight 26 kg. Vitals: Temp 38.9 C, HR 116 bpm, RR 20/min, SpO2 99%. Enlarged erythematous tonsils with whitish exudates, tender anterior cervical lymph nodes, no cough or rhinorrhea. Chest clear, abdomen soft. Treated for presumed bacterial pharyngotonsillitis with weight-based therapy.

medications.instructions: Complete full 10-day course (~40 mg/kg/day).
Give after food for fever or pain (~10 mg/kg/dose).

Pediatrics.prescriptionNotes: Encourage cool liquids and soft foods; replace toothbrush after 48 hours of antibiotics.

Pediatrics.chiefComplaint: Three-year-old child brought by grandmother with fever and refusal to eat due to mouth sores.
Pediatrics.clinicalNotes: Weight 14 kg. Vitals: Temp 38.2 C, HR 118 bpm, RR 24/min. Three small shallow vesicles with erythematous halos on the soft palate and anterior tonsillar pillars. Hydration adequate, moist tongue, lungs clear. Supportive pain relief and cold fluids advised.

medications.instructions: Give 30 minutes before meals to ease swallowing.

Pediatrics.prescriptionNotes: Offer cold milk, yogurt, or popsicles; avoid citrus or salty foods.

Pediatrics.chiefComplaint: Ten-year-old child brought by mother with intense perianal itching at night for one week.
Pediatrics.clinicalNotes: Weight 32 kg. Vitals: Temp 36.7 C, HR 86 bpm, RR 18/min. Child well-appearing, abdomen soft and non-tender. Mild perianal excoriation from scratching. Classic nocturnal pruritus ani consistent with Enterobius vermicularis. Advised treating household contacts and strict hygiene.

medications.instructions: Give 5 ml today and repeat one 5 ml dose after two weeks.

Pediatrics.prescriptionNotes: Trim fingernails short; wash bedsheets and underwear in hot water.

Pediatrics.chiefComplaint: Five-year-old child brought by father with itchy crusted sores around the nostrils for three days.
Pediatrics.clinicalNotes: Weight 18 kg. Vitals: Temp 36.9 C, HR 102 bpm, RR 22/min. Two small superficial plaques with honey-colored crusts on the upper lip and right alar crease. No surrounding cellulitis or systemic signs. Afebrile, lungs clear. Prescribed topical antibiotic ointment.

medications.instructions: Gently wash crusts with warm water and apply thin layer.

Pediatrics.prescriptionNotes: Use separate towel and wash hands after touching lesions to prevent spread.

Pediatrics.chiefComplaint: Eighteen-month-old toddler brought by mother with runny nose, mild cough, and low fever.
Pediatrics.clinicalNotes: Weight 11 kg. Vitals: Temp 37.7 C, HR 120 bpm, RR 28/min, SpO2 99%. Active, interactive, feeding well. Clear nasal discharge, normal tympanic membranes, clear lung fields without wheezing or retractions. Advised nasal saline drops and gentle bulb suctioning.

medications.instructions: Instill before feeds and sleep; suction gently if needed.
Give only if fever causes discomfort.

Pediatrics.prescriptionNotes: Avoid over-the-counter cough or cold syrups in children under 2 years.

Pediatrics.chiefComplaint: Seven-year-old child brought by aunt with intermittent belly pain and hard stools for four days.
Pediatrics.clinicalNotes: Weight 24 kg. Vitals: Temp 36.8 C, HR 94 bpm, RR 20/min. Abdomen soft, mild left lower quadrant fullness, no guarding or rebound, normal bowel sounds. No vomiting or weight loss. Prescribed weight-appropriate osmotic laxative and increased fluids.

medications.instructions: Dissolve completely in 120 ml water or juice (0.5 g/kg/day).

Pediatrics.prescriptionNotes: Encourage regular toilet sitting after meals and high-fiber fruits.

Pediatrics.chiefComplaint: Eleven-year-old child brought by mother with sore throat, mild fever, and nasal congestion.
Pediatrics.clinicalNotes: Weight 35 kg. Vitals: Temp 37.9 C, HR 92 bpm, RR 18/min, SpO2 99%. Mild pharyngeal erythema, small tonsils without exudate, clear nasal discharge, normal ear exam, clear chest. Supportive care with analgesic and warm fluids.

medications.instructions: Give for fever or throat pain (~15 mg/kg/dose).

Pediatrics.prescriptionNotes: Rest at home while febrile and maintain good fluid intake.
